sentences.text: 1  2  2025:KER:31548  JUDGMENT Dated this the 10th day of April, 2025
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.35/2012 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Palakkad is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience,
the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 27.6.2011.

According to the petitioner, on 27.6.2011 at about 8.15 p.m., while he was riding pillion on a motor cycle, a lorry bearing registration No. KL- 48-6020 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down and as a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained injuries.
3.
The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to 2025:KER:31548 the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.2,23,000/-
4.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A4 series, B1, and C1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal dismissed the claim petition.
7. Aggrieved by the above order of the Tribunal dismissing the claim petition, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Heard Sri. Jacob Sebastian, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Smt.
Latha Susan Cherian, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
9.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance 2025:KER:31548 policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
Before the Tribunal, the petitioner has not produced any charge sheet against the 2 nd respondent and as such the tribunal dismissed the claim petition.

The learned counsel for the petitioner would argue that in connection with the above accident, two claim petitions were filed by the same counsel and in one of the cases, the final report was produced and he omitted to produce the same in this case, and that is why the claim petition was happened to be dismissed.

Before this Court, at the time of hearing, the petitioner has produced copy of the final report against the 2 nd respondent, which will go to show that the accident occurred due to the Krishnakumar R vs Ramads on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28732068/
2 negligence of the 2 nd respondent.
10.

entities.text: Krishnakumar R vs Ramads on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Standing Counsel would argue that since the petitioner has produced final report only now, the interest for the delayed period is to be denied.

However, from the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioner, it is revealed that there were two claim petitions in respect of the same accident and the counsel produced the final report in one case and omitted to produce the same in the other 2025:KER:31548 case and that is why the claim petition happen to be dismissed.
In the above circumstance, it will not be just and proper to punish the claimant by denying interest for the period of delay in producing the copy of the charge.
11. One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.

As per the claim petition, the petitioner was a salesman,
earning Rs.4,000/- per month.
12.

As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2011 will come to Rs.8,000/-.Therefore, the learned counsel prayed for fixing the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.8,000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

Since the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2011 will come to Rs.8000/-, in order to award just and reasonable compensation, in the light of a dictum laid down in the 2025:KER:31548 decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra), the notional income of the petitioner is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.8,000/-.
13.

In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"(1) pain and swelling over (R) knee, (2) Post tibial spike fracture (R)"
From Exhibit A3 discharge summary, it is revealed that in the accident, the petitioner sustained fracture of right tibia.
Petitioner was treated as inpatient for 3 days.
However, he has not produced any disability certificate and as such he is not entitled to get any compensation on the head loss of disability.
14. Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, he might have lost his job at least for a period of four months.

Therefore, towards loss of earnings he is entitled to get a sum of Rs.32,000/-.(8000x4).
15.
The petitioner sustained serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 3 days.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone 2025:KER:31548 by the petitioner, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.35,000/-
towards 'pain and sufferings', Rs. 20,000/- for 'loss of amenities of life', Rs.1000/- towards transportation charges, Rs.500/- towards damage to clothing', Rs.13,312/- for medical expenses,
Rs.2000/- for 'extra nourishment' and Rs.1,000/- towards bystander expenses.
Krishnakumar R vs Ramads on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28732068/
3 16.
Therefore, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs1,04,812/-, as stated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

Sl.
 No. Head of Claim Amount Awarded in Appeal  (in Rs.)

1 Loss of earning 32,000/- (8000x4)
 2 Transport to hospital 1,000/-
 3 Damage to clothing 500/-
 4 Medical expenses 13,312/-
 5 Extra nourishment 2000/-
 6 Bystander expenses 1,000/-
 7 Pain and suffering 35,000/-
 8 Loss of amenities of life 20,000/-

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.1,04,812/- (Rupees one lakh 2025:KER:31548 four thousand eight hundred and twelve only), along with interest @ 8% per annum, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
18.
On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.

Sd/-
C. PRATHEEP KUMAR, JUDGE sou.
